text.p: Dutch retail and business services company Vendex said Monday it planned a 2.5 billion-franc ($473 million) takeover of French temporary employment agency BIS, creating a corporation with a more pan-European focus.
Analysts welcomed the deal, saying it fit well with the Dutch company's corporate strategy, and predicted growth in the French temporary employment market in coming years.
In Amsterdam, Vendex shares soared more than 10 percent to 84.90 guilders ($48.32) before closing at 81.80 ($46.56), still up 5.00 guilders ($2.85).

"Vendex is aiming for wider European coverage for temporary work and, as such, it is a good step. It looks like a good price they are willing to pay for BIS," said Keith Wills, analyst at brokerage Goldman Sachs' London office.
The acquisition will more than double annual turnover of Vendex's business services division to more than 6 billion guilders ($3.4 billion).
It will create Europe's third largest temporary employment agency and the Continent's second biggest in commercial cleaning, with 50,000 full-time employees.

Vendex said it planned an initial public offering (IPO) for the newly created services group, which will include its units Vedior, Abilis, FAA and Markgraaf, once Vedior had finalised its acquisition of BIS.
This will be followed by Vendex splitting into two independent entities. Shareholders will receive separate retail and services shares.

Vendex Chairman Jan-Michiel Hessels said Vendex's retail and services components were big enough and had significantly different growth strategies to justify a demerger, only 18 months after its initial listing.
Analysts were positive over the demerger plans.
